describeText: An agentic assistant that can decide its own steps, call internal systems and commit the firm to supplier orders without a checkpoint.

answers.In a sentence or two, what will it do fo: It works through procurement tasks by itself, calls our internal systems and places supplier orders.
answers.Where does the AI come from?: Something a team in your firm built for this job
answers.What kind of AI is it? If more than one: An AI agent that works through tasks on its own, using other tools or systems — e.g. sends messages, books things, updates records, changes code
What information will it see or use? Tic: Confidential firm information — internal data, code or documents not meant for outside the firm, whether or not they’re marked confidential
answers.What happens with what it produces? If i: acts entirely by itself, with no person involved at any point
answers.What does it do when it acts?: Something else — sends, books, updates records, deploys changes
answers.Which of these does it help decide, if a: Which suppliers to order from, and committing the firm to those orders.
answers.If it gets something wrong, can the mist: No — once it happens, it can’t be taken back
What can it get into by itself? Tick all: It has its own logins, passwords or access tokens for other systems
answers.How widely will it be used?: My team, as part of normal work

didntUnderstand.quote: Nudge screen: 'We found no words about: ... What happens with what it produces', and the checklist tick on 'Where does the AI come from — words found'
didntUnderstand.why: I wrote 'without a checkpoint', which is about what happens with the output, yet it says no words were found. It also says words were found about where the AI comes from, and I never said that. I can't tell how my words are matched to topics.

didntUnderstand.quote: Who ends up seeing or receiving what it produces, in its final form? ... Clients or customers — including people applying to us
didntUnderstand.why: My orders go to outside suppliers, and no option covers suppliers or other outside parties. Clients, the public and other teams all fit badly, so I chose 'Not sure'.
I wasn't sure whether supplier purchase orders count as 'trades'. I read it as financial trading and picked 'Something else'.

didntUnderstand.quote: acts entirely by itself, with no person involved at any point
didntUnderstand.why: I ticked it, but it says more than I wrote. I said no checkpoint beforehand. I didn't say nobody ever looks at the logs afterwards, and 'at any point' might include that.

didntUnderstand.quote: Where does the AI come from? — This tells us where your information will go.
didntUnderstand.why: It's unclear whether 'the AI' means my agent or the language model underneath it, which may be an outside model. The answer could differ.

didntUnderstand.quote: Step bar: '← Similar checks', '4 Questions', '5 Confirm'
didntUnderstand.why: I never saw a Similar checks step, and I don't know what the arrow means. I also don't know why there is a separate 'Questions' step after 'Your answers', since the form already asks them.

expectNext: When I press Continue it should check that every required question is answered and every suggestion is ticked or changed. It then moves to step 4 (Questions), probably follow-ups based on my answers, because an agent acting with no checkpoint raises more concerns. After that comes a Confirm step and a Result that says whether I can go ahead as built and what must be fixed first. I expect it to say no as it stands, and to ask for things like human approval before orders or spending limits.
ticksMean: 'I've checked this answer' means I read the AI helper's suggestion and agree with it, and I take responsibility for it. Until I tick it, the answer doesn't count and I can't continue. It does not mean the AI is correct, and it isn't a sign-off from the firm.
comment: As a developer I could follow almost all of it. The gaps were that the topic checklist doesn't match what I wrote, no option fits suppliers as the audience, and the step bar is confusing.
